quote: “But man is not made for defeat. A man can be destroyed but not defeated.”
source: Ernest Hemingway, The Old Man and the Sea, unchaptered, after the first shark (Santiago) (Scribner, 1952)
speaker: Santiago

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg Canada plain text of The Old Man and the Sea, produced from the 1952 Charles Scribner’s Sons edition
evidence.edition: The Old Man and the Sea, Charles Scribner’s Sons, New York, 1952
evidence.locator: Unchaptered; Santiago speaks it aloud after killing the mako, the first shark, and losing the harpoon

reason: The two spoken sentences are in the 1952 Scribner text exactly as proposed, split only by “he said”, which is dropped as narration. Santiago says them aloud after the first shark, so he is named as speaker.
